players.product: SMR designer - Doosan Enerbility forging/material supplier and prospective module manufacturer

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 results (CFO): revenue of $0.6 million for the three months ended March 31, 2026 versus $13.4 million a year earlier. The decrease was primarily due to RoPower technology licensing revenue recognized in the first three months of 2025 and the Fluor FEED phase II engineering work for RoPower, which was completed in late 2025. CFO: 'This quarter, we did not have revenues associated with projects'; management expects revenue and operating cash flow from sales of products and services as projects progress.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $0.6 million in Q1 2026 vs $13.4 million in the prior-year period

quarterly_data.signal: Liquidity and capital (CFO): overall liquidity stood at $1 billion at March 31, 2026 and rose to over $1.2 billion by early May 2026, to fund supply chain and manufacturing readiness and commercialization obligations. Share count rose mainly from selling 3.2 million Class A shares through the at-the-market program in Q1, generating $37.9 million in gross proceeds. Fluor completed the sale of its remaining NuScale shares, which the CFO called 'removing a significant overhang on our equity'; Fluor earned a 4.3x return on an initial investment of $570 million.
quarterly_data.figure: liquidity $1 billion at March 31st, 2026; over $1.2 billion by early May 2026; 3.2 million ATM shares for $37.9 million gross proceeds

quarterly_data.signal: Opex and cash flow outlook (CFO): Q1 opex was 'about, I think, $55 million' and is expected to rise as NuScale nears commercialization, driven by supply chain readiness and design finalization; the balance sheet was planned to absorb the extra spend. The CFO said 'I hope to be operationally cash flow positive by the end of this year' and that 'we won't be talking in terms of burn rate by the end of this year'. Accounts payable fell mainly because the stage-one payable under the partnership milestone agreement (PMA) had been recognized when the term sheet was signed.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 2026 OpEx 'about, I think, $55 million' (CFO, hedged); expected to go up

quarterly_data.signal: TVA / ENTRA1 catalyst: in September of last year TVA announced an agreement with ENTRA1 for up to 6 GW of 24/7 baseload energy using NuScale SMR technology, and ENTRA1 told NuScale that talks with TVA are 'advancing well toward a definitive PPA'. CFO: 'We're hopeful that TVA can come across the line at some point later this year.' After the PPA, NuScale expects COLA (site-specific licensing) and pre-FEED work and support for ENTRA1's supply chain. It has been working on the structure of an OEM contract to finalize quickly once the PPA is set. TVA is the 'primary focus', but ENTRA1 has a pipeline of other projects and is also considering non-PPA models such as a development structure. ENTRA1 was the only developer named in the $550 billion U.S.-Japan framework agreement. The CEO met the Korean government about a proposed $350 billion Korean investment in U.S. strategic industries, of which $200 billion would go to sectors such as nuclear power, AI and semiconductors.
quarterly_data.figure: TVA-ENTRA1 agreement for up to 6 GW; U.S.-Japan framework $550 billion; Korea $350 billion with $200 billion for nuclear/AI/semiconductors

quarterly_data.signal: Revenue expected after the PPA (CFO): NuScale expects site-specific, pre-OEM services once ENTRA1 signs a PPA with TVA, and used RoPower as the example. For RoPower over 2024 and 2025 (technology licensing, pre-FEED and FEED phase II) the CFO first said 'we realized about $8 million worth of revenue', then cited 'about $1 million' and 'about $80 million' for the same work in later answers, so the call gives no consistent amount. OEM contract structure: staged payments starting when the OEM agreement is signed and continuing through NPM manufacturing to delivery, with NuScale acting 'essentially a pass-through' from ENTRA1 (the buyer of NPMs) to its supply chain. The CFO expects the net of milestone-three PMA payouts and the first OEM payment to be cash-flow positive, and says total milestone payments can be recouped over NPM delivery.

Supply chain readiness: last month NuScale held its annual supplier working group with 37 key supplier partners to align on 2026 demand signals and near-term deployment milestones. The COO said the Houston summit drew 'over 120, 130 people', representing 'well over half of our supplier base'. NuScale is pursuing a deliberate multi-sourcing strategy for critical components to reduce single-source dependence 'in a constrained global market'. Key NuScale Power Module components remain in active production at Doosan Enerbility. The CFO cited long-standing Japanese and Korean supply-chain and equity relationships 'through IHI and through Doosan'. On domestic-content requirements for tax credits, the CCO said large-scale forgings are one area where the industry 'has fell short' on U.S. supply, and that where supply is inadequate it can be compensated from externally, with 'alternatives and ways to get past that'.
quarterly_data.figure: 37 key supplier partners at the annual supplier working group; over 120, 130 people at the Houston summit

quarterly_data.signal: Fuel supply (COO/CEO): NuScale modules run on commercial low-enriched uranium (LEU), which the COO called 'not a risk area. It's not a bottleneck', unlike HALEU. Fuel partner Framatome supplies from multiple sites: Richland, Washington in the U.S., Lingen in Germany, and a facility in France. NuScale is in preliminary fuel design with Framatome and started early so it can support market needs. The COO said: 'we don't see any bottlenecks or any kind of shortcomings there because we got ahead of it early'. Framatome asks to be kept informed on the market and customer base so it can plan capacity.

RoPower (Doicesti, Romania): Nuclearelectrica shareholders voted to advance the project, and in February the Romanian government approved the investment decision. Fluor is the primary EPC contractor and NuScale is a subcontractor to Fluor. The FEED was finished in November. Fluor is still negotiating the next 'pre-EPC' phase, which would last approximately 15 months if pre-EPC financing is secured. The COO said 'The lion's share of that will go to most likely to Fluor', and NuScale's sub-scope and revenue are not yet defined. Weekly meetings continue with the Department of Energy, RoPower, Nuclearelectrica and Fluor.
quarterly_data.figure: pre-EPC phase approximately 15 months (if financing secured)

quarterly_data.signal: Demand color: the CEO said hyperscalers are 'the elephant in the room' demanding behind-the-meter energy, and that 'The demand pull right now that we're seeing is unlike anything I've ever seen.' He described a dinner with 'a potential company that's looking at mega gigawatts here in the United States' and said 'we think we're hopeful that we're close to closure.' NuScale is the only nuclear technology the NRC has approved for behind-the-meter operation with an emergency planning zone limited to the site boundary, so plants can sit next to hyperscaler data centers. Dry air-cooled condensers cut water use by more than 90% compared with wet cooling towers. Standard design approvals cover both the 50 MW and 77 MW modules.
